found.recommendation:
Yes: on light honesty, fixed-8 can replace live.

Live's gold horn comes from a reflection-only card that sits partly above the ceiling, and its glowing cabinet comes from the shadow-ray shortcut. Fixed-8 has neither. Every light in it is a bar fixture or a photographer's light, out of frame and under the ceiling, and the two new opal panels are real lit panels that the camera can see.

At the next render:

2. For strictness, raise mantle-front about 0.25 m out of the camera's line.
3. Set 'camera': true on the 14 shot lamps.

found.summary:
Fixed-8 is honest throughout in everything that reaches the picture, and it can replace live on light honesty.

How I checked:
- I read fixed8.shot.json, fixed8.log and the audit against the scene code (lights.py, render.py) and diffed the shot against fixed-7.
- I projected every lamp, every softbox part and both panels with the scene's camera. The camera model matches the render's own part boxes.
- I looked at the frame at 1600, 800 and 168 px and in crops.

What I found is right:
- The changes are exactly the ones listed.
- Caustics are on, clamp is 0 and filter_glossy is 0.
- The shortcut is gone: 0 links left, now checked after every prop. There is no horn card.
- All 14 lamps and all five softbox and panel meshes are where the shot says. The lamps and the three softboxes are out of frame and under the ceiling. The two opal panels are in frame and seen directly, as practicals.
- The near panel's edge lands where the pale strip is. It reads as a slightly cool grey, not warm, which keeps the horn's hue true: about 100, against the studio front's 97-100.
- The far softbox's grid and flag cut softly, and its grey screen in the far horn is gone.

One new rig fault: the moved far softbox hangs where two pendant cords hang. The orange pendant's cord goes through its skirt and grid, and the red one's through its top flag. It is invisible in the picture, but no photographer could rig the box there.

Smaller points:
- The emitter list and the equipment audit do not cover the 14 shot lamps or the softbox bodies. Geometry does, and all of them are out of frame. The 14 lamps keep the engine default of being unseen by camera rays, which changes no pixel.
- mantle-front shines through the camera's position; this was already the case in live.
- A new caustic streak with sparkle dots shows on the ceiling at full size.

My files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b67/critic-lights/.

verdicts.reasoning:
Confirmed, and fix is the right severity. The remedy is bigger than the critic says.

My model: I built my own softbox model (face centred on its position, aimed like lights.aim(), a 0.1 m body behind, a 0.3 m skirt forward). It gives the log's z ranges for all five boxes: prop 20 3.363-3.397, prop 21 2.453-3.361, prop 22 2.413-3.397. A flag tilted 20 degrees up would reach z 3.558, above the log's 3.397, so the flag runs along the box's axis or level.

The cords: my projection puts them at u 148.1, 227.4, 252.3, 359.9 and 379.7 px. The dark lines in the frame are at 148, 227, 252, 360 and 379-380 px.
- Orange cord (7.66, 4.17): 8.8 cm inside the box's side edge. It is inside the skirt from z 2.88 (29.6 cm in front of the face) to z 3.30 (10.8 cm), and leaves through the skirt's top wall and the flag.
- Red cord (7.3, 4.28): 11.2 cm inside the box's floor plan if the flag runs along the axis (it crosses the flag at z 3.14), 17.5 cm if the flag is level (at z 3.35).
- Amber cord (6.92, 4.16): misses the flag tip by only 6.8 cm (along the axis) or 0.4 cm (level).
None of this shows in the picture: the cords leave the frame at z 2.27, and the nearest box part is 184 px outside it.

What I refute is the size of the fix. I kept the box at the same height and re-aimed it at the same target:
- To clear every cord by 10 cm it must move 28.5 cm (flag along the axis) or 32.5 cm (level). For 15 cm it must move 35.5-39 cm. The move is almost straight back toward the seats.
- Its throw then grows from 3.12 m to 3.29-3.34 m, which leaves 88-90 % of today's light on the far bay at strength 28, and its aim turns 4-5 degrees.
- So 'the light would be the same' is untested. The box's current spot was chosen for the far horn's mirror image (P3) and the ceiling spill (P4).

Also: in my model the far box's lower back corner comes within about 1 cm of the near box. A 30 cm move opens that gap to about 19 cm.

verified.recommendation_check:
I agree with the verdict: on light honesty, fixed-8 is far better than live and can replace it. Live's gold horn and glowing cabinet come from tricks. Fixed-8 has no horn card and 0 shadow-ray links, every set emitter has all ray visibility on, the render settings are the honest ones, and every out-of-frame lamp and softbox part is outside the frame and under the ceiling. I checked all of this myself.

What I would change:
1. The far softbox item. Clearing the cords by 10-15 cm means moving the box about 30 cm, not a hand's width: 28.5-32.5 cm for 10 cm of clearance, 35.5-39 cm for 15 cm, almost straight back toward the seats, re-aimed at the same target. That lengthens its throw from 3.12 m to about 3.3 m, which leaves about 90 % of today's light on the far bay at strength 28, and turns its aim 4-5 degrees. 'The light stays the same' is a guess, and the box's current spot was chosen to keep its image out of the far horn (P3) and its spill off the ceiling (P4). So check the moved box on a crop of the far bay and the ceiling before a re-render replaces fixed-8. The move also opens the gap to the near box, whose corner the far box nearly touches now (about 1 cm in my model), to about 19 cm.
2. Add track-bay1: move it about 10 cm toward the wall so it clears the ceiling panel. This is the critic's own L4(b), but it is missing from the to-do list.
3. Raise mantle-front 0.25-0.35 m. At 0.25 m the beam's edge still grazes the camera.
4. 'None of these changes what the picture shows' is true for items 2 and 3 and for the camera flag, but untested for the far-box move. That should not stop live coming down, but say so plainly.
5. Give the ceiling streak's dots to the photo critic.

The owner sentence overstates in two places:
- 'The one slip': there are three placement slips, and none shows. The far photo light hangs through two lamp cords. The small light behind the seat would put the camera's shadow on the Mantle. One ceiling spot sits inside the ceiling light panel.
- 'A hand's width': the move is about 30 cm.

Suggested sentence: "Fixed-8 uses no tricks, so on honesty it can replace the live picture; three of its lights sit where a real shoot couldn't put them exactly (the far photo light hangs through two lamp cords, a small light behind the seat would put the camera's shadow on the Mantle, and a ceiling spot sits inside the ceiling light), none of it shows in the picture, and the next render moves them, the far light by about 30 cm, which we check on a test crop first."

found.summary: I looked at fixed-8 at 1600, 800 and 168 px beside live, fixed-7 and the studio front, and measured it in Lab with the scene mask. It reads as a real evening bar at all three sizes, and nothing new reads as CG at 800 or 168. The near Tropos reads as a lemon loudspeaker. 40 % of the horn is lemon at the product's hue (99 vs 97), darker like the rest of the room (L* 31 vs 53), and the same colour as the cabinet. The rest is the black niche seen through clear acrylic, so the horn is two-tone at 1600. It still holds together as one clear horn, and at 800 it looks like the studio horn. The lit back reads as a pale backlit shelf back, not glare, but it renders cool blue-grey, not warm. P3 is fixed. P4 and P6 are better. The cone band (old P5) got stronger (lower third L* 19.7 -> 35.0), and a new sparkly streak sits on the ceiling. Both show at full size only. verdicts.reasoning:
Seen at 1x and 2x: the lower flank carries a mottled green-yellow cloud with a smooth, cool white rim under it, clearly stronger than in fixed-7. At 800 it is a pale green-white crescent that reads as a sheen on a glossy cone. Crops: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b67/critic-photo-verify/q1-cone-live-f7-f8-2x.png and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b67/critic-photo-verify/q1-cone-1x-f7-f8.png.

The fixed-8 numbers reproduce exactly:
- lower third L* 35.0, with 31.4 % above L* 50;
- brightest 10 %: L* 73.6, a* -2.3, b* -1.0;
- middle band: L* 42.2, C* 27.6, hue 115 by median, still greener than the cabinet's 98;
- disc r<60: L* 7.0; studio cone: 21.0.

Correction to the live and fixed-7 numbers. The critic used the fixed-8 mask on all three frames, but the near Tropos sits 14 px further left in live and fixed-7 (it moved 2 cm). Cross-correlating the woofer gives dx -14, dy 0 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b67/critic-photo-verify/v1_shift.py). Corrected for the shift:
- lower third L*: live 56.2 / fixed-7 23.2 / fixed-8 35.0;
- share above L* 50: 65.8 / 13.7 / 31.4 %.
So the rise from fixed-7 is +12 L*, not +15, and the green-yellow pixel count rises about 1.7x, not 3x.

The lane's '16.4 -> 21' is the cone's lower half. By that measure fixed-7 reads 16.5, the 2 cm crop (crop8-mv3) reads 21.2, and the full fixed-8 reads 25.7. The full frame is stronger than the lane reported.

The band does not come from the opal backs. The 5 cm black-horn crop without panels reads the same as the 5 cm crop with panels (lower flank L* 37.3 against 37.2; /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b67/critic-photo-verify/q1-test-tiles-cone-3x.png). Expect it in the 2 cm black-horn version too.

The rim: #FFE2C0 is about 4640 K, so at the 4000 K white balance it renders cool, as the opal back does. A rough mirror estimate from the lower-left flank (cone slope assumed about 28 degrees) lands on the near softbox's face, so that softbox is the likely source. A render has not confirmed it.

The mottling is a render tell at 100 %; at 800 the band reads as a believable sheen. That makes it fix.

Seen at 3x and 8x: a pale streak along a ceiling plank with five near-white dots and one yellow dot. Live and fixed-7 have only the dim, warm plank glint there. Crops: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b67/critic-photo-verify/q2-ceil-3x-live-f7-f8.png and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b67/critic-photo-verify/q2-ceil-f8-8x.png.

Reproduced exactly:
- box max L* 20.5 / 23.4 / 92.8;
- 40 px above L* 60;
- peak sRGB (247,231,227) at (442,80).
The near-white peaks are at (442,80), (429,79), (426,72), (443,84) and (411,78); the yellowish one is at (417,83), b* 15.7.

Correction on its look at 800: it is not a faint smear like the older glint. It is brighter (max L* 89.6 against the old glint's 55.9, with 12 px above L* 50) and keeps two or three specks (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b67/critic-photo-verify/q2-ceil-800-f8-x3.png). It is still small, in a dark corner, and reads as a ceiling glint, so I keep it at fix.

Where it falls: the engine's level, lens-shifted camera puts (442,80) on the 3.40 m ceiling at (5.02, 5.51, 3.40), just left of the far niche (x 5.13 to 5.97). I checked this camera model against the opal panel's edges (see Q3).

What throws it, as an estimate, not confirmed by a render:
- A flat-ceiling mirror at that spot looks at the top of the shelving, not at a lamp.
- Hot dots plus one lemon dot look like caustic light (caustics are on) bounced off or through the far Tropos's lemon acrylic, not yet settled by the samples.
- The far softbox, now aimed at the far Tropos at strength 28, fits the geometry: its light can reach the spot off an up-and-forward-facing surface such as the far horn's lower inner flare.
- The new far opal back is the other candidate.

The light is honest; the sparkles are the fault.

Reproduced exactly:

Seen: the horn is two-tone, the rim runs all round, and it holds together as one horn at 1600. At 800 it is a lemon horn with its left side dark. At 168 it is a lemon block with a black dot, while fixed-7's horn vanishes. 'Right two thirds' is fair for width (about 71 %). By area, lemon is 40 %; the driver and the top band take the rest.

The hue sits on the studio's (99 against 97), so a buyer is not misled about the colour.

Seen at 3x: a flat, pale blue-grey back under the horn and to its right, with the horn's posts and the driver body silhouetted against it. It reads as a lit shelf back at 1600 and 800, and as a faint line at 168. Why it renders cool: #FFE2C0 is about 4640 K (McCamy), cooler than the render's 4000 K white balance. The bar's track heads (#FFD2A0, about 3920 K) and house lights (#FFC890, about 3570 K) are warmer.

Two small corrections:
- 'The only cool bright surface' overstates it. The cone's white rim (a* -2.3, b* -1.0) and the triangle print's white (b* -1.0) are slightly cool too. The back is the coolest and largest; the record wall (b* +7) and the sleeves (b* +1.7) are warm.
- 'Its edges never show' is not quite right. Its top edge shows as the square top of the 5 px strip at y 68 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b67/critic-photo-verify/q4-panel-top-edge-6x.png). Its left and top edges also show through the horn as the lemon area's edges (Q3). Neither reads as a lamp.

Agreed: warming the back would pull the horn from h 99 toward orange, so recheck the hue if it is warmed.

The far Tropos did not move (shift 0, 0), so the fixed-8 mask is valid for it.

Reproduced exactly: mean L* 19.9 / 19.0 / 7.4, and lemon share 43.0 / 0.6 / 1.1 %.

The grey, screen-like patch is gone (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b67/critic-photo-verify/q5-far-horn-4x-f7-f8.png). Grey pixels (C* below 8, L* above 20) make up 39.1 % of the horn in fixed-7 and 6.8 % in fixed-8.

- The sight line to the panel's right part crosses the right cheek's plane at y about 5.95, inside the cheek.
- Sight lines through the far horn reach the left cheek (x 5.13) before they reach the back.
So the far back is hidden and adds no lemon.

Left over: a small grey fleck at the horn's right edge beside the cheek, about 8 x 12 px around (524, 355), L* 55, b* +3. It is warm, so it is not the opal back, and it is tiny (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b67/critic-photo-verify/q5-far-grey-patch-8x.png).

At 800 the far horn is a dark wedge with two white streaks. It reads black, which the owner sentence should not ignore.

At 5x, fixed-8 shows three or four soft blobs where fixed-7 has more, smaller ones (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b67/critic-photo-verify/q7-far-batt-5x-f7-f8.png).

My L* grid of the band's left interior runs smoothly from 79 to 97 in fixed-8, against fixed-7's 82 to 95 with dips. Both keep a bright blob right of the slot (x 512-518, y 409-415).

A band-pass standard deviation is not lower in fixed-8, but that measure takes in the band's edges. So 'smoother' is a visual call, and I share it only for the band's left part.

At 800 the band is about 27 x 15 px and the blobs vanish.

Reproduced (live / fixed-7 / fixed-8): mean L* 0.4 / 0.9 / 3.5, p90 0.3 / 0.9 / 9.6, and b* -1.5 in fixed-8.

Seen at 3x: a framed dark rectangle with a cloudy, cool interior and a ledge under it. It reads as a dark window or a switched-off screen, is believable, and is barely visible at 800 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b67/critic-photo-verify/q8-left-rect-3x-live-f7-f8.png).

Its cool cast points to a #FFE2C0 source. By my geometry, neither opal back can be seen from that wall; each is hidden by its niche's left cheek. So it is not their mirror image. The far softbox's new aim and strength is the likely cause, but I could not confirm it.

verified.recommendation_check:
I agree with the main call. Live must come down because of its tricks, and fixed-8 is honest. Q1 and Q2 show mostly at 100 % and are not reasons to hold. Do not call the opal back warm, and keep the horn on the studio hue.

What I would change:

1. **The black-horn side of the comparison is not evidence yet.**
   - 'Loses it in the 168 px tile' comes from fixed-7, which has the speaker in its old position and the old far softbox.
   - The 2 cm black-horn crop has not come in, and a crop cannot be judged at 168 anyway.
   - Show the owner both pictures at the same crop window and scale, plus fixed-7's 168 tile labelled as the stand-in for the black-horn version.
   - Describe the black-horn version only after the crop has been seen.

2. **Q1 does not help choose between the two.** The 5 cm black-horn crop without panels has the same cone band (lower flank L* 37.3 against 37.2), so expect the band in both versions.

3. **Correct the numbers.**
   - For the near speaker, the critic measured live and fixed-7 with the fixed-8 mask. That speaker sits 14 px further left in live and fixed-7.
   - Corrected cone lower third: live 56.2, fixed-7 23.2, fixed-8 35.0.
   - The lane's 'about 21' for the lower cone came from the 2 cm crop. The full frame reads 25.7 by the same measure.

4. **Add two points for a later render.**
   - Q2 is brighter at 800 than the critic said (peak L* 90, against the old glint's 56), so it should be the first fix.
   - In Q3, the lemon area's edge is crisp, and it is the panel's own edge, which my projection matches within about 5 px.
   - A lit back filling the whole back of the niche, as real backlit shelves are built, would give the horn about 13 % more lemon width and a thinner dark top band. Only the left fifth, in front of the cheek, would have to stay dark.

5. **The owner sentence is wrong in one place and leaves out two things.**
   - Wrong: the horn is dark on its left side and along its top, not only on its left side.
   - Missing: it never tells him a new light was added. Under his honest-light rule he should hear in plain words that each speaker shelf now has a lit back panel.
   - Missing: the far speaker's horn also looks dark.

Suggested text:

"Fixed-8 looks like a real photo of a bar at night. Each speaker shelf now has a softly lit back panel, the kind a real bar could fit; you can see it as a pale grey strip beside and under the horn. Lit from behind, the clear horn shows its lemon colour. It looks dark on its left side and along its top, where the shelf's black lining is behind it, and the far speaker's horn looks dark too. I would use it in place of the current picture. [Add this only after the 2 cm crop has been seen:] The version without the lit backs makes the horn look like black glass. Two small flaws show only up close, a greenish smear on the woofer and a sparkly spot on the ceiling, and a later render can fix them."
